features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
The deal: Three years, $52.5 million Grade: D+

We've had two significant signings off the free agent market so far, and both involve freshly minted ex-Milwaukee Brewers: After Jake Bauers landed with the Boston Red Sox on Friday, the Chicago White Sox plucked Dustin May off the championship Milwaukee pitching staff.

Whereas Boston was banking on Bauers' 2026 breakout being his current true talent level, the White Sox are perhaps taking a bigger gamble that May's past five years do not represent his real level of ability.
Since his early shine as a top Los Angeles Dodgers prospect, which included some promising early work in the majors, May's career has been journeyman-like.
Around injuries that cost him the 2024 season, he has put up 0.9 bWAR with a 91 ERA+ over 356 big-league innings for the period covering 2022 through last season.
May became a fallback addition for the Brewers at the 2026 trade deadline after more glitzy pursuits (ahem, Tarik Skubal) fell short.

features.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Joe Burrow takes QB lead, Chuba Hubbard continues rise
features.desc: Need to make or assess a trade offer? With six teams on their bye week, these rankings are designed to help.
body: Move over, Josh Allen; there's a new top fantasy QB in town, and he plays for the Cincinnati Bengals.

There's a lot of movement at running back with Chuba Hubbard, Blake Corum and Tony Pollard earning more confidence from managers, and the early returns on Justin Jefferson's reunion with Kirk Cousins has him moving up the board.

Here is my latest fantasy football rankings update for the rest of the season by position to help you identify trade values and long-term adds and drops. You'll find the top 100 at the bottom of this column.

Rankings changes: Joe Burrow and his managers are enjoying a historic run as he has accounted for four or more touchdowns in five consecutive games and scored at least 28 fantasy points in four straight.

With a friendly schedule the rest of the way, Burrow passes Josh Allen for the top spot in the rankings. The other big move is Drake Maye (ankle) leaving the top 10 as Tommy DeVito subs for him. Sad emoji.
Later, Deshaun Watson, Jacoby Brissett and Cam Ward move up to QB2 range.

Rankings changes: No, Christian McCaffrey does not usurp the top spot after his 46.3-point outing in Week 10 (Jahmyr Gibbs scored 44.2 points!), but he does move to No. 3, sliding past Bijan Robinson, who has reached 18 points in one of the past six games and remains in the top five.

Jonathan Taylor leaves the top five. Chuba Hubbard continues his rise, as do Blake Corum and Tony Pollard in RB2 territory. Emmett Johnson becomes a solid flex option, while Seth McGowan and Kaelon Black are close. Welcome back, Omarion Hampton.

features.headline: How Vikings got Kirk Cousins ready to win on short notice
features.desc: Cousins and coach Kevin O'Connell deferred to each other until they each needed to take control Sunday.
body: EAGAN, Minn. — In their first season together with the Vikings in 2022, Kevin O'Connell and Kirk Cousins developed a decidedly polite Minnesotan relationship.

O'Connell, the head coach, worried about inadvertently insulting Cousins, his quarterback. In an interview with ESPN that season, Cousins recalled O'Connell telling him he was throwing the ball well in practice — but quickly adding that his praise did not mean he hadn't thrown well on other days.
Cousins, meanwhile, was super courteous about imposing on O'Connell's busy days as a first-time head coach, offensive playcaller and father of four, including a newborn daughter.
At times that season, Cousins waited for O'Connell to invite him into meetings before he would ask scheme questions or make game-plan suggestions.

That polite tap dance resumed last week when the two were reunited at the trade deadline, a personality mix that contributed heavily to the Vikings' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers. Cousins finished 21-of-31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.
O'Connell said this week that he initially planned a light schematic burden because "I did not want him coming in here feeling like the weight of the world was on his shoulders in Week 1."
Cousins, meanwhile, acknowledged he worried about balancing his own ideas with overstepping his boundaries as a new player on the team.
"I've changed playcallers 11 times," Cousins said. "So it's this dance of when am I going to speak up and say, 'I'm not comfortable with that.

features.headline: The clock is ticking on Steph Curry's final act with the Warriors
features.desc: At 38, Curry is still brilliant — but managing his body has become the biggest battle of his career.
body: LATE LAST JANUARY, during an off-day workout in an empty downtown Minneapolis arena, Stephen Curry's right knee started bothering him.
Four days prior, he had been named an All-Star starter for an 11th time, averaging 27.2 points on extreme efficiency, keeping the Golden State Warriors' record at a respectable 25-21.
But his co-star, Jimmy Butler, had torn his right ACL the week before. Curry, at 37, was again dealing with overloaded schemes and an increased offensive burden. His knee started barking.
"That was the moment where I started to get concerned," Curry said. "It just didn't feel right."
Curry attempted to play through what he described as "a weird soreness and pain that didn't go away."

Despite being initially listed as questionable, he had 26 points against the Timberwolves, rested for a game and then scored 27 in Utah to close the road trip and 23 against the Detroit Pistons once the team returned home.
But neither the pain nor concern would subside.

"Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, 'Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'" Curry said. "And I was just faking it for the first whatever [25 minutes]."

There's something poetic about his final sequence before he left the game. Curry came off a third-quarter pindown into an isolation against Ausar Thompson and did what he described as "a high-step thing because it hurt so bad in that moment."

After the fidget, Curry shook Thompson with a crossover combination, hobbled into the lane and poured in an and-1 floater over one of the best perimeter defenders in the world to give him 23 points in those 25 minutes.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The Chicago White Sox are in agreement with free agent pitcher Dustin May on a three-year, $52.5 million deal, source confirms to ESPN.
Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Reliever Ryan Walker went to the Milwaukee Brewers in a trade that sent right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry to the San Francisco Giants.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.
Jacob Young agreed to terms on a long-term contract with the Washington Nationals, president of baseball operations Paul Toboni announced.
Source: Detroit Tigers agree to one-year deal with reliever Emilio Pagan.
RHP Ryan Weiss agrees to $1.85M deal with San Diego Padres, sources say.

features.headline: Miami Dolphins backup QB Kyle McCord showed poise in debut vs. Indianapolis Colts
features.desc: Miami coach Jeff Hafley praised McCord's poise and the trust he showed in receivers Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas.
body: All things considered, his teammates and coaches say, Kyle McCord's NFL debut showed promise.

The 2025 sixth-round pick completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards in his first career start Sunday, and scored a 3-yard rushing touchdown in a 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. It was also McCord's first game action with Miami, which traded for him in August after the preseason ended.
Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said he appreciated McCord's demeanor, particularly after Indianapolis recovered a strip sack in the end zone to take a 21-7 lead on the opening play of the second half.
"Love his composure. I like our team's composure and resiliency, and I thought Kyle was a great example of that today," Hafley said Sunday. "Things didn't always go right.
We came out in the half, and they had a defensive score, and that could have been ugly with the score.
And we fought all the way back, and Kyle did a great job, I thought there, so there's going to be some positives, and there's going to be some things that we need to correct.
"But for his first outing, I thought he kept his composure, which was really, really important to me."

McCord's outing featured a handful of marquee plays; he completed a 31-yard pass to Malik Washington that had just a 20.9% completion probability, according to Next Gen Stats. Washington tracked the ball with one hand and came down with the catch near the sideline.
The former Syracuse and Ohio State product also completed a 38-yard pass to Caleb Douglas on third-and-13 that set up his rushing touchdown two plays later.
